prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: 2024年重点信息化项目执行情况汇总表 (language zh-CN).
Grid: 5 columns × 6 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "项目" · longest unbreakable word 22px · one-line width 215px
  col 2: header "负责人" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 46px
  col 3: header "预算（万元）" · longest unbreakable word 60px · one-line width 92px
  col 4: header "进度" · longest unbreakable word 48px · one-line width 373px
  col 5: header "风险说明" · longest unbreakable word 38px · one-line width 1830px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 720px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 719px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 720px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

Your previous reply was rejected: no JSON in reply. Reply again with ONLY the JSON object.

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"An executive summary for comparing 2024 key IT projects: each row is a project, and readers need to see who owns it, its budget, how far execution has progressed, and what risk remains.","reading":"Readers scan row by row, using 项目 as the row anchor, then take in the short metadata 负责人 and 预算（万元）, then read the narrative status in 进度 and 风险说明. Budgets and progress markers are compared across rows; risk notes are read as prose after the status.","groups":["col 1 项目 is the row identifier/anchor and must stay visually dominant enough to distinguish rows.","col 2 负责人 and col 3 预算（万元） are short factual metadata; they should be compact and stable so they do not steal width from prose.","col 4 进度 and col 5 风险说明 are the narrative/status pair; they belong together as the flexible, wrapping part of the table, with 风险说明 taking more width because its text is much longer."],"keep_intact":["Project names and quoted/proper identifiers such as “一网通办”, platform names, and trial-site names; avoid breaking inside quotation marks or Latin acronyms.","Owner names, preferably on one line.","Budget figures including commas and decimals, e.g. 1,280.00; never split a number.","Progress markers such as 60%, 88%, 3个, 10月, UAT, and dates; keep numbers with their units."],"may_wrap":["Long project names between Chinese characters, except inside quoted names.","Progress prose between clauses or Chinese characters.","Risk notes freely as multi-line prose.","Column headers such as 预算（万元） and 风险说明, which can wrap without harming scanning."]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[166,68,84,196,205],"idea":"Balanced publication layout: keep owner and budget compact, give 项目 enough room for most names, and split the remaining width fairly evenly between progress and risk."},{"name":"B","widths":[146,68,84,158,263],"idea":"Risk-led layout: accept more wrapping in project and progress so the very long risk commentary gets the widest readable measure and fewer lines."},{"name":"C","widths":[190,68,84,150,227],"idea":"Project-led layout: prioritize intact project identification and a generous risk column, while letting progress wrap into a compact status block."]}

{"understanding":{"purpose":"A one-page management summary of 2024 IT project execution: each row is a project, and readers check owner, budget, progress narrative and risk note together — the table is read row-by-row for status, and column-by-column only for budget or risk comparisons.","reading":"The eye enters at the project name (the row's identity), jumps right to 预算 for the money figure, then reads 进度 and 风险说明 as two prose fields that carry the actual status story. 负责人 is a small lookup field consulted occasionally, so it should be narrow but still show the full name on one line. Because the two prose columns are long, rows are already multi-line tall, so wrapping there costs nothing; the project name and the budget figure are what must stay legible at a glance.","groups":["col 1 项目 — row identity, must anchor each row","col 2 负责人 — short lookup attribute of the row, sits next to the project name","col 3 预算（万元） — numeric comparison column, must stay whole and right-aligned in feel","col 4 进度 and col 5 风险说明 — twin prose fields, both naturally wrap, should be sized as a pair rather than independently"],"keep_intact":["预算（万元） header (60px unbreakable) and all budget figures such as 1,280.00 — never split or wrapped","负责人 header and the 3-character names on one line","项目 names: at minimum no mid-word break of identifiers like “一网通办”, “信创迁移”; ideally whole on one or two lines","进度/风险说明: keep phrases like “UAT 测试计划”, “3 个试点处室迁移”, “60%” unbroken"],"may_wrap":["项目 names (2 lines acceptable)","进度 sentences (already multi-line in every row)","风险说明 paragraphs (very long, will always wrap to many lines — the main absorber of width)"]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[210,68,100,175,166],"idea":"Row-unit balance: give 项目 almost its full one-line width so each project name reads as a single anchor, keep 负责人 and 预算 intact, and split the remaining space evenly between the two prose columns."},{"name":"B","widths":[160,68,100,195,196],"idea":"Comparison-first: compress 项目 to a controlled two-line wrap and pour the savings into 进度 and 风险说明 so the status and risk text of adjacent rows can be scanned and compared side by side."},{"name":"C","widths":[140,68,96,155,260],"idea":"Risk-led hierarchy: treat 风险说明 as the primary content and let it dominate, accepting a narrow three-line project name and a tight 进度 column as the price of a readable risk narrative."}]}
